Lesson 23: Stateful Mission Runner & Human-in-the-Loop UI Gates

Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Design and code a stateful Mission Execution Finite State Machine (FSM) in Python.
  2. Implement Human-in-the-Loop UI Gates that suspend autonomous execution until human confirmation is received.
  3. Expose interactive gate state to the Web Cockpit and ESP32-S3 Smartwatch Badge over WebSockets and REST.
  4. Process asynchronous user responses (respond_to_ui_interaction) and transition the DAG to the selected conditional branch.
  5. Demonstrate full mission execution lifecycle with automated node status tracking.

1. The Mission Runner Finite State Machine (FSM)

An autonomous mission runner cannot be a blocking script. It must be an asynchronous event-driven state machine:

MERMAID
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> IDLE
    IDLE --> RUNNING_NODE: Start Mission(DAG)
    
    state RUNNING_NODE {
        [*] --> ExecutingNav
        [*] --> ExecutingDelay
        [*] --> ExecutingDock
    }
    
    RUNNING_NODE --> WAITING_UI_INPUT: Node is 'ui_interaction'
    WAITING_UI_INPUT --> RUNNING_NODE: Human selects Option (Web / Watch)
    WAITING_UI_INPUT --> FAILED: UI Timeout Exceeded
    
    RUNNING_NODE --> RUNNING_NODE: Node Success -> Next Node
    RUNNING_NODE --> PAUSED: Operator triggers Pause
    PAUSED --> RUNNING_NODE: Operator triggers Resume
    
    RUNNING_NODE --> COMPLETED: Next Node is NULL (Exit)
    RUNNING_NODE --> ABORTED: E-Stop / Critical Error
    
    COMPLETED --> IDLE
    FAILED --> IDLE
    ABORTED --> IDLE

2. Implementing the Mission Runner (mission_runner.py)

Create level2/scripts/mission_runner.py with an asynchronous execution loop:

PYTHON
"""
Stateful Mission DAG Runner with Human-in-the-Loop UI Interaction Gates
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import time
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger("mission_runner")

class MissionState:
    IDLE = "IDLE"
    RUNNING = "RUNNING"
    WAITING_UI_INPUT = "WAITING_UI_INPUT"
    PAUSED = "PAUSED"
    COMPLETED = "COMPLETED"
    FAILED = "FAILED"
    ABORTED = "ABORTED"

class StatefulMissionRunner:
    def __init__(self, gateway_client):
        self.client = gateway_client
        self.state = MissionState.IDLE
        self.current_mission: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
        self.current_node_id: Optional[str] = None
        self.active_ui_interaction: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
        self.ui_response_future: Optional[asyncio.Future] = None

    async def start_mission(self, mission_dag: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Initialize and begin execution of a validated mission DAG."""
        if self.state not in (MissionState.IDLE, MissionState.COMPLETED):
            return f"Cannot start: Mission runner is currently in state {self.state}."

        self.current_mission = mission_dag
        self.current_node_id = mission_dag["start_node_id"]
        self.state = MissionState.RUNNING
        logger.info(f"Started mission '{mission_dag.get('name')}' at node '{self.current_node_id}'")

        # Spawn non-blocking execution task
        asyncio.create_task(self._execution_loop())
        return "Mission started successfully."

    async def _execution_loop(self):
        nodes_map = {n["id"]: n for n in self.current_mission["nodes"]}

        while self.state == MissionState.RUNNING and self.current_node_id:
            node = nodes_map.get(self.current_node_id)
            if not node:
                logger.error(f"Node '{self.current_node_id}' missing from mission definition.")
                self.state = MissionState.FAILED
                break

            node_type = node.get("type")
            logger.info(f"Executing node '{self.current_node_id}' (Type: {node_type})")

            # Execute according to node type
            next_node = None
            if node_type == "navigation":
                next_node = await self._exec_navigation_node(node)
            elif node_type == "delay":
                next_node = await self._exec_delay_node(node)
            elif node_type == "ui_interaction":
                next_node = await self._exec_ui_interaction_node(node)
            elif node_type == "dock":
                next_node = await self._exec_dock_node(node)
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Unknown node type '{node_type}'. Skipping.")
                next_node = node.get("next_node_id")

            # Check termination
            self.current_node_id = next_node
            if not self.current_node_id:
                logger.info("Terminal node reached. Mission COMPLETED.")
                self.state = MissionState.COMPLETED
                break

    async def _exec_navigation_node(self, node: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
        wp_id = node.get("params", {}).get("waypoint_id")
        logger.info(f"Navigating to waypoint '{wp_id}'...")
        # Dispatch to gateway
        resp = await self.client.post("/api/v1/navigation/navigate_to_waypoint", json={"waypoint_id": wp_id})
        # Simulate awaiting Nav2 arrival
        await asyncio.sleep(2.0)
        return node.get("next_node_id")

    async def _exec_delay_node(self, node: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
        duration = node.get("params", {}).get("duration_seconds", 1.0)
        logger.info(f"Settling for {duration} seconds...")
        await asyncio.sleep(duration)
        return node.get("next_node_id")

    async def _exec_ui_interaction_node(self, node: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
        params = node.get("params", {})
        self.active_ui_interaction = {
            "node_id": node["id"],
            "title": params.get("title", "Action Required"),
            "prompt": params.get("prompt", ""),
            "options": params.get("options", ["Confirm"]),
            "timestamp": time.time()
        }
        self.state = MissionState.WAITING_UI_INPUT
        self.ui_response_future = asyncio.get_event_loop().create_future()

        logger.info(f"Suspended execution. Waiting for operator input: '{params.get('prompt')}'")

        try:
            # Wait for response with timeout
            timeout = params.get("timeout_seconds", 120)
            selected_option = await asyncio.wait_for(self.ui_response_future, timeout=timeout)
            logger.info(f"Operator responded: '{selected_option}'")
            self.state = MissionState.RUNNING
            self.active_ui_interaction = None

            # Resolve next node from conditional transitions
            transitions = node.get("conditional_transitions", {})
            return transitions.get(selected_option, node.get("next_node_id"))
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            logger.error("UI Interaction timed out. Mission marked FAILED.")
            self.state = MissionState.FAILED
            self.active_ui_interaction = None
            return None

    def submit_ui_response(self, option: str) -> bool:
        """Invoked when operator responds via Web Cockpit or ESP32 Smartwatch."""
        if self.state == MissionState.WAITING_UI_INPUT and self.ui_response_future:
            if not self.ui_response_future.done():
                self.ui_response_future.set_result(option)
                return True
        return False

3. Human Interaction Flow on Web Cockpit and ESP32 Smartwatch

When the Mission Runner enters WAITING_UI_INPUT:

  1. It broadcasts a WebSocket event to all connected clients:
JSON
{
  "event": "ui_interaction_active",
  "data": {
    "node_id": "gate_operator_inspection",
    "title": "Pallet Inspection",
    "prompt": "Operator: Confirm parts are loaded onto tray.",
    "options": ["Confirmed", "Reject / Empty"]
  }
}
  1. The Web Cockpit pops up an interactive modal card in the bottom navigation tray.
  2. The ESP32-S3 Smartwatch Badge vibrates on the warehouse worker's wrist and displays the prompt with tactile physical buttons:
  • Button 1 (Top): Selects "Confirmed"
  • Button 2 (Bottom): Selects "Reject / Empty"
MERMAID
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Runner as Stateful Mission Runner
    participant Web as Web Cockpit (Browser)
    participant Watch as ESP32-S3 Smartwatch Badge
    actor Worker as Warehouse Worker

    Runner->>Runner: Arrives at Node 'gate_operator_inspection'
    Runner->>Runner: State -> WAITING_UI_INPUT
    Runner-->>Web: WS Event: ui_interaction_active
    Runner-->>Watch: MQTT / WS Notification: "Pallet Inspection"
    
    Watch->>Worker: Wrist Haptic Vibration + Screen Awake
    Web->>Worker: Modal Dialog Rendered on Screen
    
    Worker->>Watch: Taps "Confirmed" Button on Wrist
    Watch->>Runner: POST /api/v1/ui/interaction/respond {option: "Confirmed"}
    Runner->>Runner: Future Resolved with "Confirmed"
    Runner->>Runner: Transition to 'nav_to_storage'
    Runner-->>Web: WS Event: ui_interaction_cleared
    Runner-->>Watch: Notification Cleared (Status: In Transit)

4. Testing the Full Interactive Gate Loop

You can simulate the entire gate sequence in Python without physical hardware:

PYTHON
# Simulate Mission Runner execution
runner = StatefulMissionRunner(gateway_client=mock_client)
await runner.start_mission(mission_dag)

# Check active prompt
assert runner.state == MissionState.WAITING_UI_INPUT
print(f"Active Prompt: {runner.active_ui_interaction['prompt']}")

# Simulate worker tapping 'Confirmed' on their wrist badge
runner.submit_ui_response("Confirmed")

# Execution resumes autonomously!
await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
assert runner.state == MissionState.RUNNING

Summary

  • Stateful mission execution requires a decoupled asynchronous Finite State Machine.
  • ui_interaction nodes allow physical AMRs to safely collaborate with human warehouse workers.
  • The state machine suspends execution deterministically until a response is submitted from the Web Cockpit or ESP32 Smartwatch Badge.
  • In Lesson 24, we bring all three days together in the End-to-End Grand Capstone Fleet Pipeline!

quizzes.prompt: How does a 'HumanApprovalGate' step function in a stateful mission execution graph?
options: It terminates the mission immediately
It pauses mission progression, presents a prompt/alert to an operator via web or edge badge, and waits for explicit approval before resuming autonomous execution
It overrides the robot's LiDAR sensors

Lesson 24: Day 3 & Grand Capstone — End-to-End Enterprise Fleet Pipeline

Learning Objectives

By the end of this capstone lesson, you will be able to:

  1. Integrate all layers built across Level 2 into a single unified Industrial AMR Control & Intelligence Pipeline.
  2. Trace an end-to-end command from Natural Language Voice/Chat → Frontier AI Agent → MCP Server → Safety Guard → FastAPI Gateway → ROS 2 Nav2 → Web Cockpit → ESP32 Smartwatch Badge → Precision Docking.
  3. Execute and verify the complete Grand Capstone Automated Integration Test Suite.
  4. Deploy the software stack seamlessly onto both the Level 1 Gazebo simulation and the physical NavPro Mini AMR.
  5. Receive your enterprise robotics practitioner graduation credentials.

1. The Unified Enterprise Architecture

Here is the complete software and hardware topology you have designed, implemented, and verified:

    subgraph Human & AI Reasoning Layer
        User[Human Supervisor Voice / Chat] --> Frontier[Frontier AI Model: Claude / Gemini / Antigravity]
        Frontier <-->|JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio / SSE| MCP[NavPro MCP Server :8000]
    end

    subgraph Deterministic Safety Layer
        MCP --> Safety[Pre-flight Deterministic Safety Interceptor]
        Safety -->|Validated & Clamped| API[FastAPI Enterprise Gateway :8000]
    end

    subgraph ROS 2 Actuation & Control Plane
        API --> ROS2Exec[High-Concurrency MultiThreadedExecutor]
        ROS2Exec --> Nav2[Nav2 Action Client: NavigateToPose]
        ROS2Exec --> MicroROS[Micro-ROS Motor Driver & Sensors]
    end

    subgraph Live Operator Cockpit Layer
        API -->|20Hz WebSocket Telemetry| Cockpit[Web Cockpit Canvas SLAM UI :8000]
        API -->|Active UI Gate Event| Watch[ESP32-S3 Smartwatch Badge]
        Watch -->|Wrist Button 'Confirmed'| API
    end

    subgraph Physical Actuators & Simulation
        Nav2 --> Gazebo[Gazebo Harmonic Simulation (Level 1)]

    end

Every single component in this diagram is now backed by production-grade Python, JavaScript, and ROS 2 code written by you.

2. The 12-Step End-to-End Grand Capstone Scenario

Let's trace how the complete pipeline behaves in real-time during an enterprise shift transfer:

    Operator->>AI: "Prepare Shift Transfer: Inspect Assembly Bay 1, await worker loading confirmation, then return to dock."

3. The Grand Capstone Automated Verification Script

To verify that your entire Level 2 system operates flawlessly, execute the automated verification suite level2/scripts/verify_grand_capstone.py:

PYTHON
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Level 2 Grand Capstone Verification Suite
Validates the complete chain: REST Gateway -> Safety Interceptor -> MCP Server -> Mission Runner -> Web Cockpit.
"""

import sys
import asyncio
import httpx
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s")
logger = logging.getLogger("capstone_verifier")

GATEWAY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

async def run_capstone_verification():
    logger.info("==================================================")
    logger.info("🚀 STARTING LEVEL 2 GRAND CAPSTONE VERIFICATION")
    logger.info("==================================================")

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=GATEWAY_URL, timeout=10.0) as client:
        # Step 1: Health & Telemetry Check
        logger.info("[Test 1/6] Verifying REST Gateway Health & Telemetry...")
        resp = await client.get("/api/v1/telemetry")
        assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200, got {resp.status_code}"
        telem = resp.json()
        logger.info(f"✅ Telemetry verified: Pose ({telem.get('x', 0):.2f}, {telem.get('y', 0):.2f}), Battery {telem.get('battery_soc', 100):.1f}%")

        # Step 2: Waypoint Registry Verification
        logger.info("[Test 2/6] Verifying Semantic Waypoint Store...")
        resp = await client.get("/api/v1/waypoints")
        assert resp.status_code == 200
        waypoints = resp.json()
        logger.info(f"✅ Waypoint store active with {len(waypoints)} registered landmarks.")

        # Step 3: Safety Interceptor Geofence Rejection
        logger.info("[Test 3/6] Verifying Deterministic Safety Interceptor (Out-of-Bounds Rejection)...")
        bad_goal = {"x": 999.0, "y": 999.0, "yaw": 0.0}
        resp = await client.post("/api/v1/navigation/navigate_to_pose", json=bad_goal)
        assert resp.status_code in (400, 422), f"Expected safety rejection, got HTTP {resp.status_code}"
        logger.info("✅ Safety barrier successfully intercepted out-of-bounds coordinate!")

        # Step 4: Waypoint Navigation Dispatch
        logger.info("[Test 4/6] Verifying Non-blocking Nav2 Navigation Dispatch...")
        resp = await client.post("/api/v1/navigation/navigate_to_waypoint", json={"waypoint_id": "dock_01"})
        assert resp.status_code in (200, 202)
        task_id = resp.json().get("task_id")
        logger.info(f"✅ Navigation goal accepted. Dispatched Task ID: {task_id}")

        # Step 5: Human-in-the-Loop UI Gate Loop
        logger.info("[Test 5/6] Verifying UI Interaction Gate & Response...")
        # Simulate active interaction
        resp = await client.get("/api/v1/ui/interaction/active")
        # Submit simulated worker response
        resp = await client.post("/api/v1/ui/interaction/respond", json={"option": "Confirmed", "responder": "test_suite"})
        assert resp.status_code in (200, 404) # 200 if active, 404 if idle
        logger.info("✅ Human-in-the-loop UI response pipeline verified.")

        # Step 6: Software E-Stop Verification
        logger.info("[Test 6/6] Verifying Enterprise Emergency Stop Interlock...")
        resp = await client.post("/api/v1/safety/estop", json={"reason": "Capstone verification test", "requester": "verifier"})
        assert resp.status_code == 200
        logger.info("✅ E-Stop engaged successfully. Motor drive interlock locked.")

    logger.info("==================================================")
    logger.info("🎉 GRAND CAPSTONE VERIFICATION COMPLETED: 100% PASS")
    logger.info("==================================================")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(run_capstone_verification())

4. Graduation & Transition to Physical Hardware

Congratulations! You have completed the comprehensive Level 2: Enterprise Robotics Software & Fleet Engineering curriculum.

What You Built from Scratch:

  1. High-Performance Robotics Gateways: FastAPI REST + 20Hz WebSocket telemetry broadcasting powered by ROS 2 MultiThreadedExecutor and thread-safe mutex caches.
  2. Client SDKs & Web Cockpits: Pure JavaScript/Python SDKs, HTML5 2D Canvas SLAM rendering, 60 FPS live trajectory animation, interactive touch virtual joysticks, and SVG waypoint markers.
  3. Model Context Protocol (MCP): Native JSON-RPC 2.0 tool servers bridging frontier models directly to physical robot actions.
  4. Deterministic Safety Barriers: Pre-flight geofence validators, battery reserve guards, and velocity clamps preventing AI hallucinations from causing physical damage.
  5. Industrial Mission DAGs: Stateful finite state machine runners supporting human-in-the-loop UI gates across web cockpits and wearable smartwatch badges.

Deploying to the Physical NavPro Mini AMR:

To deploy this exact stack to your physical robot:

  • Clone your gateway and MCP server to the AMR's on-board computer (Raspberry Pi 5 / Jetson Orin Nano).
  • Set ROBOT_GATEWAY_URL="http://192.168.1.50:8090".
  • Launch your MCP server in Antigravity or Claude Desktop.
  • The physical robot will execute the exact same missions, dock with the same precision, and push the same interactive alerts to your smartwatch badge!
